history.dynasty: British colonial period (constructed under a British officer, Lt. Col. Stanley Smith)
history.summary: Paat Baba Mandir is a Hanuman temple on a small hill near the Gun Carriage Factory (GCF), Vidya Nagar, Jabalpur. Local legend says that when British officer Lt. Col. Stanley Smith's factory walls kept collapsing at night, Hanuman appeared in his dream and told him an idol lay buried at the site; workers unearthed a Hanuman idol wrapped in a red cloth ('pat' in Hindi), and temple construction began on 12 August 1903, after which the factory was completed without incident. Special aarti is performed every Tuesday at 7:30 PM. The complex also has shrines to Durga and Shiva plus garden areas. Coordinates are from the geocoder; one AI-listing source places the temple ~10 km away at 23.172472, 79.977902, so the location is approximate (verify).

town_description: Jabalpur is a major city in Madhya Pradesh on the banks of the Narmada, famous for the marble rocks and Dhuandhar falls at Bhedaghat. It was an important British cantonment and arms-manufacturing centre (Gun Carriage Factory, ordnance factories). Today it is the region's educational, administrative and industrial hub.
